title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is seeing a flurry of activity, from funding rounds to strategic partnerships, as companies gear up for a competitive landscape. Meanwhile, government initiatives are pushing for advancements in propulsion and space computing, hinting at a more integrated approach to space operations.

themes.title: Funding Frenzy in Space
themes.body: True Anomaly's recent $190M Series C and Impulse Space's $500M Series D highlight a growing investor appetite for space ventures. With SpaceX eyeing a $75 billion IPO, the financial stakes are clearly rising.

themes.title: Nuclear Propulsion Developments
themes.body: NASA's efforts to streamline its nuclear electric propulsion demo mission signal a serious commitment to advanced propulsion technologies. This could pave the way for more ambitious deep-space missions, assuming they can avoid the usual bureaucratic delays.

themes.title: Data Centers in Orbit
themes.body: The concept of orbital data centers is gaining traction, with AstroForge's DeepSpace-2 spacecraft and Muon Space's new satellite design aimed at this market. As data demands increase, the race to establish infrastructure beyond Earth is heating up.

themes.title: International Space Dynamics
themes.body: China's institutional framework for space computing and recent allied workshops in The Hague indicate a push for global collaboration and competition in space resilience. Meanwhile, Russian activities near commercial GEO slots are a reminder that geopolitical tensions remain a constant in this arena.
